seeds.goal: You can answer a friend's letter: react to their news, tell your own, ask two questions and close warmly.
seeds.why: An informal letter is the most tested A2 genre — and the one where students forget to answer the questions they were asked.
seeds.ex: Aliya answered a pen-friend's letter point by point. Her partner wrote: 'you are the only one who answered everything'.
seeds.read: Read the letter and find one thing: what news does Aliya react to first?
seeds.task: Answer a letter from your friend (60–90 words): thank them, react to their news, tell two pieces of your own news, ask two questions and close warmly.
model: Thanks for your letter — it arrived on my birthday, which was perfect.
I am really glad your exams went well; you worked hard for them.
As for me, I have started swimming twice a week.
Add a second piece of news
My family also moved to a new flat near the park, so I have my own room at last.
What are you doing in the summer? Are you still learning Spanish?
Write soon and send photos! Love, Aliya.
phr: It was great to hear from you.
Было здорово получить от тебя весточку.
I was sorry to hear about …
sent: Thanks for your letter, it arrived on my birthday.
I am really glad your exams went well.
As for me, I have started swimming twice a week.
My family moved to a new flat near the park.
I have my own room at last.
What are you doing in the summer?
I have not been to the new cinema yet.
We can meet in August if you come.
My brother is much taller than me now.
Write soon and send some photos.
topics: I have started swimming twice a week and my family moved to a new flat.
Two things have changed since my last letter.
Your exams went well and you got into the group you wanted.
Your news made my week.
What are you doing in the summer? Are you still learning Spanish?
There are two things I want to know.
ideas: Two pieces of my own news
A long description of my school building
My opinion about the postal service
seeds.title: An informal letter
seeds.sub: Answering your friend's news

seeds.goal: You can describe a person so that a reader could recognise them: appearance, character, habits and one short story that proves it.
seeds.why: Describing people is where adjectives, word order and relative clauses meet. One story at the end is what makes the description true.
seeds.ex: Ruslan described his football coach for a class blog. Three readers said they knew exactly the type of person he meant.
seeds.read: Read the description and find one thing: what story proves that the coach is patient?
seeds.task: Describe a person you know well (60–90 words): who they are, what they look like, what they are like, one habit, and a short story that shows their character.
model: I want to describe my football coach, Sergey Petrovich.
He is a tall man in his fifties with grey hair and very quick eyes.
He always wears the same blue jacket, in summer and in winter.
He is patient but he never lets anybody be lazy.
He arrives twenty minutes before every training session.
Last year he spent two hours with our worst player, and now that boy is in the first team.
Say what you think of them
He is the only adult who never shouts at us.
phr: The person I know best is …
Человек, которого я знаю лучше всех, — …
He is a tall man with …
What I like about her is …
Что мне нравится в ней, так это …
He is the kind of person who …
I learned a lot from her.
sent: He is a tall man with grey hair.
He always wears the same blue jacket.
He is patient but he never lets anybody be lazy.
He arrives twenty minutes before training.
Last year he spent two hours with our worst player.
That boy is now in the first team.
He does not shout at us when we lose.
He has trained our team for eleven years.
The player who he helped is my neighbour.
He can explain a mistake without hurting you.
topics: He is tall, in his fifties, with grey hair and very quick eyes.
You would recognise him in a crowd.
He arrives early, stays late and never raises his voice.
His habits say more than his words.
He spent two hours with our worst player and that boy is now in the first team.
One story explains this man completely.
ideas: Who the person is to me
A story that shows their character
The history of our football club
seeds.title: Describing a person
seeds.sub: Looks, character and one story

seeds.goal: You can describe a place: where it is, what you see, hear and smell there, what people do and why it matters to you.
seeds.why: Weak descriptions use 'beautiful' three times. Strong ones use three concrete details — and that skill transfers to every level above.
seeds.ex: Dana described the Green Bazaar for a travel blog. The editor kept it because of one line about the smell of dried apricots.
seeds.read: Read the description and find one thing: what does Dana notice first at the market?
seeds.task: Describe a place you know well (60–90 words): where it is, what you see and hear there, what people do, the best time to go, and why it matters to you.
model: The Green Bazaar is in the centre of Almaty.
The first thing you notice is the smell: dried apricots, fresh bread and coriander.
Long tables are covered with red apples and enormous bags of nuts.
Everybody is talking at the same time in three languages.
Old women taste the cheese before they buy a single piece.
The best time is early on Saturday, before the crowds arrive.
I go there with my grandmother, and for me it is the sound of the city.
phr: The first thing you notice is …
The best time to go is …
sent: The Green Bazaar is in the centre of Almaty.
The first thing you notice is the smell.
Long tables are covered with red apples.
Everybody is talking at the same time.
Old women taste the cheese before they buy it.
The best time is early on Saturday.
I have visited this market since I was five.
The sellers do not like people who only look.
We bought two kilos of dried apricots there.
It is much cheaper than the supermarket.
topics: Dried apricots, fresh bread and coriander — you smell the market before you see it.
The market starts with a smell.
Old women taste the cheese, sellers shout prices and nobody is quiet.
The bazaar is a place of noise and negotiation.
Go early on Saturday, before the crowds and before the best nuts are gone.
Timing changes the whole experience.
ideas: The history of the whole city
What I bought there last year
seeds.title: Describing a place
seeds.sub: A place through details, not adjectives

seeds.goal: You can tell a story: set the scene, tell what happened in order, describe the problem and finish with the result.
seeds.why: A story is where the past simple and past continuous finally start to mean different things, and where linking words earn their place.
seeds.ex: Arman wrote a story about a lost phone for a school competition. It won because the last sentence was one line long.
seeds.read: Read the story and find one thing: how did Arman get his phone back?
seeds.task: Write a short story (70–100 words) about a day when something went wrong: set the scene, tell what happened in order, describe the problem and finish with what happened in the end.
model: Set the scene: when and where
It was a hot Friday in July and I was going to the airport.
I was listening to music on the bus and thinking about my holiday.
When I got off, I realised that my phone was not in my pocket.
For a minute I could not breathe.
I ran back to the bus stop and asked three people about the bus number.
Then a woman called my name: the driver had found the phone under the seat.
Since that day I always check my pocket twice.
phr: For a minute I could not …
sent: It was a hot Friday in July.
I was listening to music on the bus.
When I got off, I realised my phone was gone.
For a minute I could not breathe.
I ran back to the bus stop.
A woman called my name from the door.
The driver had found the phone under the seat.
I did not have any money for a taxi.
Since that day I always check my pocket.
It was the longest ten minutes of my life.
topics: It was a hot Friday in July and I was on the bus to the airport.
Everything started normally.
I got off, put my hand in my pocket and found nothing.
The problem appeared in one second.
The driver had found the phone under the seat and waited for me.
The story ended better than it started.
ideas: A description of the airport building
seeds.title: A short story
seeds.sub: One event, told in order

seeds.goal: You can review a place: say where it is, what you had, what was good, what was not, and who you would recommend it to.
seeds.why: A review is the first genre where your opinion must be supported by a detail. 'Nice' proves nothing; 'the soup came cold' does.
seeds.ex: Sabina's review of a student café was published on a city site. The café changed its lunch menu two weeks later.
seeds.read: Read the review and find one thing: what exactly does Sabina recommend ordering?
seeds.task: Write a review of a café or restaurant (70–100 words): where it is, when you went, what you ordered, one good thing, one bad thing, and who should go there.
model: Name the place and where it is
Coffee Point is a small café two minutes from the university.
I went there for lunch on a Tuesday with two classmates.
We ordered soup, chicken sandwiches and three coffees.
The soup was excellent — hot, fresh and cheaper than anywhere in the district.
However, we waited twenty-five minutes, and the music was too loud to talk.
Lunch for three cost 4,500 tenge, which is fair for the centre.
I would recommend it for a quick lunch, but not for a long conversation.
sent: Coffee Point is a small café near the university.
I went there for lunch on Tuesday.
We ordered soup and three coffees.
The soup was hot, fresh and very cheap.
However, we waited twenty-five minutes for the food.
The music was too loud to talk.
Lunch for three people cost 4,500 tenge.
I would recommend it for a quick lunch.
The waiter did not bring the bill for ten minutes.
It is cheaper than the café next door.
topics: We ordered soup, sandwiches and coffee, and the soup was the best part.
The food deserves most of the praise.
We waited twenty-five minutes and the music made conversation impossible.
The service is where this café loses points.
Lunch for three cost 4,500 tenge, which is fair for the centre.
The price is reasonable for the location.
ideas: One good and one bad detail
A café in another city I liked
My opinion about coffee in general
seeds.title: A café review
seeds.sub: What was good, what was not, who should go

seeds.goal: You can answer a post in public: say what you agree with, what you do not, give one reason and one example from your life.
seeds.why: A comment is short and public. It teaches you to make a point in three sentences without sounding rude.
seeds.ex: Yerbol commented on an article about school uniforms. The author replied to him and quoted his example.
seeds.read: Read the comment and find one thing: what example from his own life does Yerbol give?
seeds.task: Write a comment on a blog post about school uniforms (50–80 words): say what you agree with, what you disagree with, give one reason, one example from your life, and end with a question.
model: I agree that a uniform saves time in the morning.
Say what you do not agree with
However, I do not think it makes students equal.
Everybody still sees whose shoes and whose phone are expensive.
Give an example from your life
In my class we all wear the same shirt, and nobody has forgotten who is rich.
Admit one point on the other side
Admittedly, mornings are easier when you do not choose clothes.
Do uniforms work better in smaller schools?
sent: I agree that a uniform saves time in the morning.
However, I do not think it makes students equal.
Everybody still sees whose phone is expensive.
In my class we all wear the same shirt.
Nobody has forgotten who is rich.
Mornings are easier without a choice of clothes.
Do uniforms work better in smaller schools?
Our school changed the rules two years ago.
I have worn a uniform since the first class.
The uniform which we wear is dark blue.
topics: A uniform saves ten minutes every morning and stops arguments at home.
There is a real argument for uniforms.
Everybody still sees whose shoes and whose phone cost more.
The equality argument does not survive contact with reality.
In my class we wear the same shirt and nothing has changed.
My own school is the example I trust most.
ideas: What I disagree with, with a reason
An attack on the author personally
seeds.title: A blog comment
seeds.sub: Agree, disagree, add something

seeds.goal: You can cancel or apologise in a message: say sorry, explain briefly, offer an alternative and check that it suits the other person.
seeds.why: Cancelling badly costs friendships. Cancelling well is a formula of four sentences, and it is the same formula at work later.
seeds.ex: Nurai had to cancel a trip with a host sister. Because she offered two new dates, the trip happened a week later.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: what does Nurai offer instead?
seeds.task: Write a message cancelling plans with a friend (50–80 words): say sorry, explain why, apologise once more, offer two alternatives and ask which suits them.
model: Say the bad news at once
I am really sorry, but I cannot come on Saturday.
My grandmother is in hospital and we are going to Taraz for the weekend.
Say how you feel about it
I feel terrible because I know you booked the tickets.
Could we go next Saturday or on the Sunday after that instead?
I will pay for my ticket anyway if you cannot return it.
Tell me which day works for you. Sorry again!
phr: I will make it up to you.
sent: I am really sorry, but I cannot come on Saturday.
We are going to Taraz for the weekend.
I feel terrible because you booked the tickets.
Could we go next Saturday instead?
I will pay for my ticket anyway.
I did not know about this yesterday.
The tickets which you bought are for Saturday.
I have never cancelled our plans before.
Tell me which day works for you.
topics: My grandmother is in hospital and the whole family is going to Taraz.
The reason is a family emergency.
Could we go next Saturday, or on the Sunday after that?
There are two other dates that work for me.
I will pay for my ticket if you cannot return it.
I do not want you to lose money because of me.
ideas: A long story about my family
seeds.title: An apology message
seeds.sub: Sorry, why, and a new offer

seeds.goal: You can write to people who will host you: introduce yourself, give your arrival details, mention food or health needs and ask two questions.
seeds.why: This email decides your first three days abroad. Everything you forget to write becomes a problem at the airport.
seeds.ex: Aizhan's email listed her flight, her allergy and two questions. Her host family met her with the right food in the fridge.
seeds.read: Read the email and find one thing: what does Aizhan ask the family to tell her?
seeds.task: Write an email to your future host family (70–100 words): introduce yourself, give your arrival details, say what you eat or cannot eat, offer something, and ask two questions.
model: My name is Aizhan Nurlanova and I am sixteen. I am the student who will stay with you in July.
I live in Almaty with my parents and I study English at school and online.
My flight arrives at Manchester at 14:20 on 3 July.
Say what you need them to know
I eat everything except mushrooms, and I am allergic to cats.
I would like to cook a Kazakh dish for you one evening.
Could you tell me what the weather is like in July, and whether I need to bring a towel?
phr: I am looking forward to meeting you.
sent: My name is Aizhan and I am sixteen.
I am the student who will stay with you.
I live in Almaty with my parents.
My flight arrives at 14:20 on 3 July.
I would like to cook a Kazakh dish for you.
Could you tell me about the weather in July?
I have never travelled abroad alone.
I do not need a lot of space for my things.
topics: My flight arrives at 14:20 on 3 July at Manchester airport.
Here are my travel details.
I eat everything except mushrooms and I am allergic to cats.
There are two things you should know about me.
Could you tell me about the weather and whether I need a towel?
I have two practical questions.
ideas: The full story of my school year
seeds.title: An email to a host family
seeds.sub: Introduce yourself before you arrive

seeds.goal: You can review a film: say what it is about without spoiling it, name what is good, name what is weak, and say who would enjoy it.
seeds.why: Reviews teach you to separate description from opinion — the exact skill every higher-level essay depends on.
seeds.ex: Timur's review of a Kazakh film was printed in a school magazine. The editor changed only one word.
seeds.read: Read the review and find one thing: who does Timur think should watch this film?
seeds.task: Write a film review (70–100 words): the title and type of film, what it is about (no ending!), what is good, what is weak, and who should watch it.
model: Tomiris is a historical drama from Kazakhstan.
Say what it is about, no spoilers
It follows a young woman who becomes the leader of her people after a family tragedy.
The main actress is excellent, especially in the quiet scenes.
The landscapes and the horse scenes are the best I have seen in a local film.
However, the middle of the film is slow and some battles look repetitive.
It is closer to a slow European drama than to a Hollywood action film.
Watch it if you like history and long films; avoid it if you want two hours of action.
phr: The film tells the story of …
It follows a young woman who …
sent: Tomiris is a historical drama from Kazakhstan.
It follows a young woman who becomes a leader.
The main actress is excellent in the quiet scenes.
The landscapes are the best I have seen.
However, the middle of the film is slow.
I watched it twice last winter.
It is longer than most films in the cinema.
Do not watch it if you want pure action.
topics: It follows a young woman who becomes the leader of her people.
The story is simple to summarise.
The landscapes and horse scenes are the strongest part of the film.
Visually, the film is remarkable.
The middle hour is slow and some battles repeat themselves.
The film has one clear weakness.
ideas: The title and type of film
What it is about, without the ending
A list of other films I like
seeds.title: A film review
seeds.sub: Story without spoilers, then judgement

seeds.goal: You can explain a process: what you need, the steps in order, one warning and one tip.
seeds.why: If the reader cannot follow your instructions, the text failed — this is the clearest feedback any genre gives you.
seeds.ex: Adil wrote instructions for making a paper lantern for a school festival. Every group in the class made one correctly.
seeds.read: Read the instructions and find one thing: what mistake does Adil warn about?
seeds.task: Explain how to do something you know well (70–100 words): what it is, what you need, four steps in order, one warning and one tip.
model: Say what the reader will make or do
Here is how to make a simple paper lantern in fifteen minutes.
You need one sheet of thick paper, scissors, glue and a small candle holder.
First, fold the paper in half along the long side.
Then cut straight lines from the fold, stopping three centimetres from the edge.
After that, open the paper and glue the two short edges together.
Be careful: never cut all the way to the edge, or the lantern falls apart.
Finally, use an electric tea light instead of a real candle — paper burns quickly.
sent: Here is how to make a paper lantern.
You need thick paper, scissors and glue.
First, fold the paper in half.
Then cut straight lines from the fold.
After that, open the paper and glue the edges.
Never cut all the way to the edge.
The lantern falls apart if you cut too far.
Use an electric light instead of a candle.
I made twelve lanterns for the festival last year.
topics: Thick paper, scissors, glue and a small holder — nothing else.
The materials are simple and cheap.
Fold, cut, open, glue: the whole lantern is four movements.
The process has only four steps.
Never cut to the edge and never use a real candle.
Two mistakes ruin the lantern or the evening.
ideas: What I did at the festival
seeds.title: How to do something
seeds.sub: Instructions a stranger can follow

seeds.goal: You can write a short email asking for information: say why you are writing, ask two or three exact questions and thank the reader.
seeds.why: Vague emails get vague answers. Numbered, exact questions get exact ones — that is the whole lesson of this genre.
seeds.ex: Madina asked a language school three numbered questions. She got three numbered answers within a day.
seeds.read: Read the email and find one thing: what does Madina need to know about the price?
seeds.task: Write an email asking for information about a summer course (60–90 words): say where you saw it, why you are writing, ask three exact questions and close politely.
model: I am writing to ask about your summer English course in July.
I saw the advertisement on your website last week.
First, how many students are there in one group?
Second, does the price of 90,000 tenge include the books?
Third, do you give a certificate at the end of the course?
Thank you in advance. I look forward to your reply.
phr: I am writing to ask about …
I am sixteen and my level is …
I would like to start in …
I look forward to your reply.
sent: I am writing to ask about your summer course.
I saw the advertisement on your website.
How many students are there in one group?
Does the price include the books?
Do you give a certificate at the end?
I am sixteen and my level is elementary.
I would like to start in July.
I have not studied at a language school before.
The course which interests me starts on 5 July.
Thank you in advance for your answer.
topics: How many students are in a group and who teaches them?
My first questions are about the group.
Does 90,000 tenge include the books and the materials?
The price needs one clarification.
Do you give a certificate, and is it recognised by universities?
The certificate matters for my application.
seeds.title: Asking for information
seeds.sub: Three questions that get answers

seeds.goal: You can complain in writing: say what you bought, what is wrong, what you have already tried and what you want them to do.
seeds.why: A complaint without a request is only a bad mood in writing. The last sentence is the one that changes anything.
seeds.ex: Nurlan complained about a broken bag in eight sentences. The shop replaced it in three days.
seeds.read: Read the letter and find one thing: what does Nurlan want the shop to do?
seeds.task: Write a complaint about something you bought (70–100 words): what and when you bought it, what is wrong, what you have already done, what you want, and a deadline.
model: Say what you bought and when
On 5 April I bought a school bag in your shop in Mega Park.
After two weeks the main zip broke and one strap came off.
I still have the receipt and I have attached two photographs.
Say what you have already done
I came to the shop on Saturday, but the assistant told me to write to you.
I would like a new bag or my money back.
Could you answer within ten days? Yours faithfully, Nurlan Aliyev.
phr: I am writing to complain about …
I would like a new … or my money back.
Я хотел бы новый … или возврат денег.
… күн ішінде жауап бере аласыз ба?
I look forward to hearing from you.
sent: On 5 April I bought a school bag in your shop.
After two weeks the main zip broke.
The assistant told me to write to you.
I would like a new bag or my money back.
Could you answer within ten days?
This is the second bag which has broken.
topics: The main zip broke after two weeks and one strap came off.
Two things are wrong with the bag.
I have the receipt, two photographs and the date of purchase.
I can prove everything I say.
I would like a new bag or my money back within ten days.
Here is what I am asking for.
ideas: What I want them to do
My opinion about the shopping centre
seeds.title: A simple complaint
seeds.sub: What is wrong and what you want

seeds.goal: You can invite people to an event: give the reason, the day, the time, the place, what to bring and how to answer.
seeds.why: An invitation is a test of completeness: one missing detail and half the guests arrive at the wrong time.
seeds.ex: Aruzhan invited fifteen people to a leavers' party in English. Nobody asked her a single extra question.
seeds.read: Read the invitation and find one thing: how should the guests answer?
seeds.task: Write an invitation to an event (60–90 words): what the event is, the day and time, the place with directions, what to bring, what will happen, and how to reply.
model: We are having a leavers' party for our class on Friday, 24 May.
It starts at six in the evening and finishes at about eleven.
The party is at the Loft café on Tole Bi Street, opposite the old cinema.
There will be food, a quiz about our seven years together and a photo wall.
Please bring one old school photo and 3,000 tenge for the food.
There is no dress code, but nobody wants to see school uniform.
Answer in the group chat before Wednesday so we can book the right number of places.
phr: It starts at … and finishes at …
sent: We are having a leavers' party on Friday.
It starts at six and finishes at eleven.
The party is at the Loft café on Tole Bi Street.
There will be food, a quiz and a photo wall.
Please bring one old school photo.
Answer in the group chat before Wednesday.
We booked the café two weeks ago.
The café which we chose is opposite the old cinema.
Everybody who answers gets a place.
topics: Friday, 24 May, six in the evening, the Loft café on Tole Bi Street.
Here are the four facts you need.
There will be food, a quiz about our seven years and a photo wall.
This is what the evening will look like.
Bring an old photo and 3,000 tenge, and answer before Wednesday.
Here is what we need from you.
ideas: Who I did not invite and why
My memories of the first class
seeds.title: A detailed invitation
seeds.sub: Everything a guest needs to know

seeds.goal: You can thank somebody in writing: say what for, why it mattered, what changed because of it, and offer something back.
seeds.why: Generic thanks are forgotten in a minute. A thank-you with one specific detail is remembered for years and often gets answered.
seeds.ex: Damir thanked a volunteer teacher for one specific lesson. She sent him extra materials the same week.
seeds.read: Read the email and find one thing: which lesson does Damir mention?
seeds.task: Write a thank-you email (60–90 words): who you thank, exactly what for, why it mattered, what changed for you, and what you offer or hope for next.
model: Say thank you and what for
Thank you very much for the four weeks of speaking club.
The lesson about telephone English was the most useful hour of my year.
Last week I called a hostel in Prague myself, and the woman understood me.
For the first time I did not ask my sister to speak for me.
If you need a student to help with the beginners' group, I would be glad to come.
phr: I am writing to thank you for …
I would be glad to help.
sent: Thank you very much for the speaking club.
The telephone lesson was the most useful hour.
Last week I called a hostel in Prague.
The woman on the phone understood me.
For the first time I did not ask my sister for help.
I have never spoken English on the phone before.
I would be glad to help the beginners' group.
The club which you organised meets on Thursday.
My confidence has grown a lot this month.
I can come on Thursdays after four.
topics: The lesson about telephone English was the most useful hour of my year.
One lesson stood out from the rest.
Last week I called a hostel in Prague and the woman understood me.
The proof came a week later.
If you need help with the beginners' group, I can come on Thursdays.
I would like to give something back.
ideas: Who I thank and what for
My plans for the summer holiday
seeds.title: A thank-you email
seeds.sub: Thanks with a reason and a next step

seeds.goal: You can describe a photograph: what is in the foreground and background, what people are doing, and what you think happened before or after.
seeds.why: Photo description is a standard exam task, and it trains the present continuous plus prepositions of place better than any exercise.
seeds.ex: Alua described a family photo in an oral exam. The examiner said the guess at the end was what raised her mark.
seeds.read: Read the description and find one thing: what does Alua think happened just before the photo?
seeds.task: Describe a photograph (60–90 words): where it was taken, what is in the foreground and background, what the people are doing, how they feel, and what you think happened before or after.
model: The photo shows a family having dinner in a small kitchen.
Say what is in the front
In the foreground there is a long table covered with plates and one enormous teapot.
In the background you can see an open window and mountains.
A grandmother is pouring tea while three children are laughing at something.
One boy is holding his phone under the table, and his mother has clearly noticed.
Everybody looks relaxed, as if the meal has been going on for hours.
I think somebody has just told a joke, because nobody is looking at the camera.
phr: In the background you can see …
That is why I like this photo.
Вот почему мне нравится это фото.
It looks like a normal evening.
sent: The photo shows a family having dinner.
In the foreground there is a long table.
In the background you can see the mountains.
A grandmother is pouring tea for everybody.
Three children are laughing at something.
One boy is holding his phone under the table.
I think somebody has just told a joke.
The photo was taken in my grandmother's kitchen.
Nobody is looking at the camera.
topics: A long table, plates, an enormous teapot and eight people around it.
The foreground is full of the meal itself.
An open window and mountains behind the family.
The background tells you where this is.
Nobody is looking at the camera and everybody is laughing.
Something happened just before the photo.
seeds.title: Describing a photo
seeds.sub: What is happening and what it tells you

seeds.goal: You can write about a future job: what it is, why you want it, what skills it needs and what you are doing now to get there.
seeds.why: Every scholarship form and interview begins here. Writing it once gives you sentences you will reuse for years.
seeds.ex: Aisulu wrote about becoming a vet for a university open day. The admissions officer quoted her last sentence back to her.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what is Aisulu doing right now to reach her goal?
seeds.task: Write about your dream job (70–100 words): what it is, why you want it, what skills it needs, what you are doing now, and where you want to be in ten years.
model: I would like to be a veterinary doctor.
I chose this job because animals cannot explain what hurts, and somebody has to understand them.
A vet needs patience, strong nerves and very good biology.
Say what is hard about it
The hardest part is telling an owner that nothing can be done.
Say what you are doing now
I am volunteering at a small animal shelter every Sunday.
After school I am going to study at the agricultural university in Almaty.
Say where you want to be
In ten years I want to open a clinic in my home town, where there is none.
phr: I would like to be a …
Я выбрал эту работу, потому что …
In ten years I want to …
sent: I would like to be a veterinary doctor.
A vet needs patience and very good biology.
The hardest part is talking to the owners.
I am volunteering at an animal shelter every Sunday.
I am going to study at the agricultural university.
In ten years I want to open a clinic.
My town does not have a single vet.
I have worked with dogs since I was twelve.
The shelter which I help has forty animals.
topics: Animals cannot explain what hurts, and somebody has to understand them.
My reason is simple and it has not changed.
I volunteer at a shelter every Sunday and read biology in English.
I am not waiting for university to start.
In ten years I want a clinic in my home town, where there is none.
The goal has a place, not only a name.
seeds.title: My dream job
seeds.sub: What, why, and what it needs

seeds.goal: You can describe a journey: how you travelled, how long it took, what you saw and one thing that went wrong or surprised you.
seeds.why: Journeys give you transport vocabulary, times and the past simple in one text — and every travel conversation reuses it.
seeds.ex: Berik described a two-day train journey for a class blog. Readers asked for part two.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what surprised Berik most on the journey?
seeds.task: Write about a journey you have made (70–100 words): where you went, how you travelled, how long it took, what you saw, one problem or surprise, and how you felt at the end.
model: Last August I travelled from Almaty to Astana by train with my father.
The journey took nineteen hours in a compartment with four beds.
We left at ten in the evening and I could not sleep for the first three hours.
In the morning there was nothing outside the window but flat yellow steppe.
An old man in our compartment told us stories about the same railway in 1975.
What surprised me most was how quickly nineteen hours passed.
We arrived at five in the afternoon, tired but glad we had not flown.
phr: В прошлом … я ездил из … в …
We left at … and arrived at …
Мы выехали в … и приехали в …
sent: Last August I travelled from Almaty to Astana.
The journey took nineteen hours by train.
We left at ten in the evening.
I could not sleep for the first three hours.
In the morning there was only flat steppe.
An old man told us stories about 1975.
What surprised me most was the time.
We arrived at five in the afternoon.
I have never travelled so far by train.
The train which we took leaves every evening.
topics: Nineteen hours, four beds, one small window and endless steppe.
The train itself became part of the story.
An old man told us about the same railway in 1975.
The best part of the journey was a stranger.
We arrived at five, tired but glad we had not flown.
The end of the journey explained the choice.
ideas: What I saw on the way
The price of plane tickets in general
seeds.title: A journey
seeds.sub: Getting there, and what happened on the way

seeds.goal: You can explain a holiday to a foreigner: when it is, what it means, what people do, what they eat and what it feels like.
seeds.why: Explaining your own culture in English is the most frequent real task for a learner abroad — and the hardest to improvise.
seeds.ex: Sanzhar explained Nauryz to a partner class in Italy. They cooked nauryz kozhe from his description.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what do people eat at this festival?
seeds.task: Explain a festival in your country to a foreign friend (70–100 words): when it is, what it celebrates, what people do, what they eat, and what you personally like about it.
model: Name the festival and the date
Nauryz is celebrated on 21 and 22 March in Kazakhstan.
It is the beginning of spring and, for us, the beginning of a new year.
Before the holiday every family cleans the house and pays back small debts.
In the streets people put up white yurts, sing and play traditional games.
Everybody eats nauryz kozhe, a soup of seven ingredients that means abundance.
My grandmother makes it in a huge pot and gives it to all the neighbours.
Say what you like about it
What I like most is that on those two days nobody is a stranger.
phr: It is a soup of seven …
You should come and see it.
sent: It is the beginning of spring.
Every family cleans the house before the holiday.
People put up white yurts in the streets.
Everybody eats nauryz kozhe on these days.
My grandmother gives it to all the neighbours.
We visited five houses last year.
What I like most is the open doors.
topics: It falls on 21 March and it marks the beginning of spring and a new year.
The date and the meaning go together.
People clean their houses, pay back debts and put up yurts in the streets.
Preparation is half of the holiday.
Everybody eats nauryz kozhe, a soup of seven ingredients.
One dish belongs to this holiday alone.
ideas: When it is and what it means
The history of every holiday in the country
seeds.title: A festival in my country
seeds.sub: What it is and how people celebrate

seeds.goal: You can write an advert: what you sell, its condition, the price, why you sell it and how to contact you.
seeds.why: An advert is the shortest persuasive text there is. Every unnecessary word costs you a reader.
seeds.ex: Yerzhan sold a bike in two days with a six-line English advert on an expat board.
seeds.read: Read the advert and find one thing: why is Yerzhan selling the bike?
seeds.task: Write an advert to sell something (50–80 words): what it is, its age and condition, what is included, the price, why you are selling it and how to contact you.
model: For sale: a men's city bike, dark green, size L.
I bought it two years ago and I have used it only in summer.
It is in very good condition: no rust, new brakes, one small scratch on the frame.
The price includes a lock, a pump and a light.
I am asking 55,000 tenge, and I can go down a little for a quick sale.
I am selling it because I am moving to a city with no cycle lanes.
Write to me here or call after six in the evening.
phr: It is in very good condition.
sent: For sale: a men's city bike in dark green.
I bought it two years ago.
It is in very good condition.
The price includes a lock and a pump.
I am asking 55,000 tenge for it.
I am selling it because I am moving.
There is one small scratch on the frame.
I have used it only in summer.
I can go down a little for a quick sale.
Call me after six in the evening.
topics: Two years old, no rust, new brakes and one small scratch.
The condition is the first thing a buyer asks about.
The price includes a lock, a pump and a light.
You get more than the bike itself.
I am moving to a city with no cycle lanes.
There is nothing wrong with the bike — only with my new address.
ideas: A long story about my cycling trips
seeds.title: A for-sale advert
seeds.sub: Sell it in fifty words

seeds.goal: You can write a notice about something you lost: what it is, where and when you lost it, how to recognise it and how to reach you.
seeds.why: This genre punishes vague description immediately: 'a black bag' comes back to nobody, 'a black bag with a broken zip and a maths book inside' does.
seeds.ex: Dinara's notice described one detail — a sticker of a red fox. The bag came back the same day.
seeds.read: Read the notice and find one thing: which detail makes the bag easy to recognise?
seeds.task: Write a lost-property notice (50–80 words): what you lost, where and when, three details that identify it, what is inside, a reward if any, and how to contact you.
model: I lost it on Thursday, 14 March, between the library and bus stop number 12.
It is black with a grey front pocket and a sticker of a red fox on the left side.
Inside there is a maths textbook, a blue folder and a pair of glasses in a hard case.
The bag is old, but the glasses are new and I cannot read the board without them.
There is a small reward for the glasses.
Please call or write to 8 777 123 45 67 at any time.
sent: I lost a black school backpack on Thursday.
It happened between the library and the bus stop.
It is black with a grey front pocket.
There is a sticker of a red fox on the side.
Inside there is a maths textbook and a folder.
The glasses are new and expensive.
I cannot read the board without them.
There is a small reward for the glasses.
Please call me at any time.
I have looked for it in every classroom.
topics: Black, a grey front pocket and a sticker of a red fox on the left.
Three details make this bag easy to identify.
A maths textbook, a blue folder and glasses in a hard case.
What is inside matters more than the bag.
The glasses are new and I cannot read the board without them.
This is why I am asking for help.
ideas: A story about another lost thing
seeds.title: A lost-property notice
seeds.sub: Describe it well enough to get it back

seeds.goal: You can ask somebody for help: say what you need, why, exactly what you are asking, and make it easy to refuse.
seeds.why: A favour asked badly puts the other person in a corner. A favour asked well gives them a way out — and usually gets a yes.
seeds.ex: Anel asked a classmate to record a lesson she would miss. Because she offered a way out, the answer was yes.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: what exactly does Anel ask her friend to do?
seeds.task: Write a message asking a friend for a favour (50–80 words): what you need, why, exactly what they must do, how long it takes, what you offer in return, and how they can say no.
model: I have a dentist appointment on Wednesday and I will miss the physics lesson.
Could you record the last twenty minutes, when he explains the homework?
Say how little it costs them
You only need to press record on your phone and send me the file.
I will send you my chemistry notes from Friday — you missed that lesson too.
Give them a way to say no
If it is difficult, just tell me and I will ask Dana.
phr: I will send you … in return.
sent: I have a dentist appointment on Wednesday.
I will miss the physics lesson.
Could you record the last twenty minutes?
You only need to press record on your phone.
I will send you my chemistry notes.
If it is difficult, just tell me.
I have never asked you for this before.
The lesson which I will miss is the last one.
I do not need the whole lesson.
topics: I have a dentist appointment and I will miss the last physics lesson.
Here is why I am asking.
Press record for twenty minutes and send me the file — that is all.
The favour is smaller than it sounds.
If it is difficult, tell me and I will ask Dana instead.
You can say no without any problem.
ideas: A way for them to say no
A complaint about the physics teacher
seeds.title: Asking a favour
seeds.sub: Ask clearly and make it easy to say yes

seeds.goal: You can announce a change: say what was planned, what has changed, what the new plan is and what people must do now.
seeds.why: Half of all workplace messages are exactly this. The reader needs the new fact first, not your explanation.
seeds.ex: Bakyt sent one message about a changed rehearsal time. Fourteen people came at the right hour.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: what is the new time?
seeds.task: Write a message about a change of plan (50–80 words): what was planned, what has changed, why, the new plan, what people must do now, and who to ask.
model: The rehearsal has moved from Saturday to Sunday.
Remind people of the old plan
We were going to meet on Saturday at eleven in the school hall.
The new time is Sunday at ten, in the same hall.
The hall is used for an exam on Saturday and nobody told us until today.
Please confirm in the chat that Sunday works for you.
Say what happens if it does not
If three people cannot come, we will move the rehearsal to Monday evening.
Any questions — write to me or to Aigerim.
phr: There is a change of plan.
We were going to meet at …
sent: The rehearsal has moved from Saturday to Sunday.
We were going to meet at eleven.
The new time is Sunday at ten.
The hall is used for an exam on Saturday.
If three people cannot come, we will move it again.
The hall which we booked is the same.
I do not know why the school changed it.
Write to me or to Aigerim with questions.
topics: Saturday at eleven has become Sunday at ten, in the same hall.
The change itself is one line.
The hall is used for an exam and nobody told us until today.
The reason is not ours.
Confirm in the chat, and if three people cannot come we move to Monday.
This is what happens next.
ideas: A complaint about the school administration
A long history of our rehearsals
seeds.title: Telling about a change
seeds.sub: Something changed — tell people clearly

seeds.goal: You can write a short biography: when and where someone was born, what they did, what they are known for and why they matter to you.
seeds.why: Biography is the natural home of the past simple and of dates — and it is the format of every 'about the author' box you will ever write.
seeds.ex: Aruzhan wrote a biography of her great-grandmother for a family archive. Three relatives asked for a copy.
seeds.read: Read the biography and find one thing: what did this woman do during the war?
seeds.task: Write a short biography of a person you admire (70–100 words): when and where they were born, their early life, what they did, what they are known for, and why they matter to you.
model: Say when and where they were born
My great-grandmother Rakhima was born in 1925 in a village near Semey.
Say something about the early years
She was the oldest of seven children and left school at twelve to work.
During the war she worked as a nurse in a military hospital in Semey.
After 1945 she trained as a teacher and taught in the same village school for forty years.
She had five children, and all of them finished university.
Say what she is remembered for
In the village she is still remembered as the teacher who never lost a student.
Say why she matters to you
I have her photograph on my desk because she started with nothing and changed everything.
phr: During the war she worked as …
That is why she matters to me.
Вот почему она важна для меня.
I have her photograph on my desk.
Её фотография стоит у меня на столе.
sent: Rakhima was born in 1925 near Semey.
She was the oldest of seven children.
She left school at twelve to work.
During the war she worked as a nurse.
After 1945 she trained as a teacher.
She taught in the same school for forty years.
All of her five children finished university.
She is still remembered in the village.
I have her photograph on my desk.
She started with nothing and changed everything.
topics: Born in 1925, oldest of seven, out of school at twelve.
Her early life explains everything that followed.
A nurse during the war, then a village teacher for forty years.
She had two careers, both of them in service.
In the village she is still remembered as the teacher who never lost a student.
Her reputation outlived her.
ideas: When and where they were born
A turning point in their life
A list of every relative I have
seeds.title: A short biography
seeds.sub: A life in seven sentences

seeds.goal: You can write about being ill: what the problem is, how long it has lasted, what you have done and what you need now.
seeds.why: Being ill abroad is when your English matters most. This text is the written version of that conversation.
seeds.ex: Miras wrote to a school nurse in Poland. Because he listed his symptoms and dates, he was seen the same morning.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: how long has Miras been ill?
seeds.task: Write a message about your health (50–80 words): what is wrong, since when, what you have already done, what you cannot do because of it, and what you are asking for.
model: I have had a sore throat and a temperature since Monday evening.
This morning the temperature was 38.2 and I could not eat breakfast.
I have taken paracetamol and drunk a lot of tea, but nothing has changed.
I do not think I can sit through six lessons today.
Could I see the school doctor this morning, or should I go to the clinic?
phr: I do not feel well today.
Могу ли я попасть к врачу …?
Should I go to the clinic?
sent: I have had a sore throat since Monday.
I could not eat any breakfast.
I have taken paracetamol and drunk tea.
I do not think I can sit through six lessons.
Could I see the school doctor this morning?
My mother called the clinic at eight.
The medicine which I took did not help.
I will bring a note from the doctor tomorrow.
topics: A sore throat and a temperature since Monday evening, 38.2 this morning.
Here are my symptoms and the dates.
I have taken paracetamol and drunk a lot of tea, with no result.
I have already tried the simple things.
Could I see the school doctor, or should I go to the clinic?
I need to know what to do now.
ideas: What is wrong and since when
A story about an illness last year
My opinion about the school canteen food
seeds.title: A message about health
seeds.sub: What is wrong and what you need

seeds.goal: You can write a short news note: what happened, where, when, who took part, one quotation and the result.
seeds.why: News writing forces you to put the most important fact first — the habit that saves every text you write later.
seeds.ex: Ainur's note about a chess tournament opened the school magazine. The editor cut nothing.
seeds.read: Read the note and find one thing: who won the tournament?
seeds.task: Write a note for a school magazine about an event (70–100 words): what happened, when and where, who took part, one detail, one short quotation and the result.
model: Our school won the city chess tournament for the first time in nine years.
The tournament took place on 16 March in the Palace of Schoolchildren.
Twelve schools sent teams of four players, and our team was the youngest.
The final game lasted almost two hours and finished with three minutes on the clock.
"I stopped being afraid after the second game," said Aisultan, our first board.
The team thanks Sergey Petrovich, who trained them every Saturday since October.
In April the team will play in the regional tournament in Taldykorgan.
phr: Он екі мектеп … құрамда команда жіберді.
sent: Our school won the city chess tournament.
The tournament took place on 16 March.
Twelve schools sent teams of four players.
Our team was the youngest in the hall.
The final game lasted almost two hours.
Aisultan said he stopped being afraid.
The coach trained them every Saturday since October.
In April the team will play in Taldykorgan.
The team which won is in class nine.
topics: Our school won the city tournament for the first time in nine years.
The headline is the result itself.
Twelve schools, teams of four, and ours was the youngest.
The scale of the event explains the achievement.
In April the team plays in the regional tournament in Taldykorgan.
The story does not end here.
ideas: My own opinion about sport at school
seeds.title: A note for the school magazine
seeds.sub: News in a hundred words

seeds.goal: You can report on a trip: where you went, what you did, what you learned, one problem and whether you recommend it.
seeds.why: A report is different from a story: it keeps the facts and drops the drama. Learning the difference now saves you at B2.
seeds.ex: Dias wrote a trip report that the school used to plan the next year's visit.
seeds.read: Read the report and find one thing: what does Dias suggest changing next time?
seeds.task: Write a report about a school trip (70–100 words): where and when you went, what you did there, what you learned, one problem, and one suggestion for next time.
model: On 12 October our class of 24 students visited the Kok-Tobe observatory.
We travelled by bus for forty minutes and arrived at six in the evening.
An astronomer gave us a short lecture and then we looked at Saturn through the big telescope.
I learned that the rings of Saturn are mostly ice, not rock.
The best part was the ten minutes when the lights went off and we saw the whole sky.
The main problem was the cold: nobody told us to bring warm jackets.
Next time the school should say what to wear and book two telescopes for a big group.
sent: On 12 October our class visited the observatory.
We travelled by bus for forty minutes.
An astronomer gave us a short lecture.
We looked at Saturn through the telescope.
I learned that the rings are mostly ice.
The best part was the darkness.
Nobody told us to bring warm jackets.
The school should book two telescopes next time.
Twenty-four students waited for one telescope.
I would recommend this trip to other classes.
topics: Twenty-four students, a forty-minute bus ride and one telescope.
The numbers explain most of what follows.
A short lecture, then Saturn, then ten minutes of complete darkness.
The evening had three parts.
Nobody told us to bring jackets and one telescope was not enough.
Two things should change next year.
ideas: Who sat next to whom on the bus
seeds.title: A school trip report
seeds.sub: Where you went and what you learned

seeds.goal: You can plan something with a friend in writing: suggest a plan, give options, ask for their opinion and agree on the details.
seeds.why: Planning is negotiation. This text teaches you to suggest without deciding for the other person.
seeds.ex: Aigerim planned a weekend with a friend from Poland in five messages. Nothing was misunderstood.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: which two options does Aigerim suggest?
seeds.task: Write a message planning a weekend with a friend (60–90 words): suggest a plan, give two options, say what you prefer and why, ask about money or time, and ask them to choose.
model: Are you free this Saturday? I have two ideas for the day.
We could take the cable car up Kok-Tobe and walk down through the park.
Or we could go to the new exhibition at the Kasteyev museum, which closes next week.
Say what you prefer and why
I prefer the museum, because the forecast says rain after midday.
The tickets are 2,000 tenge for students — is that okay for you?
We could meet at the museum at eleven, or at the bus stop at half past ten.
Tell me which you prefer and I will book the tickets tonight.
sent: We could take the cable car up Kok-Tobe.
I prefer the museum because of the rain.
The tickets are 2,000 tenge for students.
We could meet at the museum at eleven.
The forecast says rain after midday.
I will book the tickets tonight.
I have not been to that museum since 2022.
Tell me which option you prefer.
topics: The cable car and a walk down, or the exhibition that closes next week.
There are two possible days here.
The forecast says rain after midday, so the museum is safer.
The weather decides this for me.
Tickets are 2,000 tenge and I can book them tonight.
The practical side is simple.
ideas: A question about time or money
A story about a museum I visited in another city
seeds.title: Planning a weekend together
seeds.sub: Suggest, ask, agree

seeds.goal: You can give written feedback: say what you did, what helped you, what did not work and what you suggest changing.
seeds.why: Feedback that only praises changes nothing. Feedback that only complains is ignored. The balance is the skill.
seeds.ex: Kanat's feedback on a summer school led to a real change in the timetable the next year.
seeds.read: Read the feedback and find one thing: what does Kanat suggest changing?
seeds.task: Write feedback on a course you have taken (70–100 words): which course and when, what you learned, what helped most, what did not work, and one clear suggestion.
model: I attended the two-week summer English course in July.
I was in the elementary group with eleven other students.
The speaking games in the first hour helped me most: I spoke more in two weeks than in a year at school.
Our teacher corrected mistakes at the end of the activity, not during it, which made everybody braver.
The grammar tests on Fridays were too long and we never had time to check them together.
I suggest making the test shorter and keeping twenty minutes for the answers.
Overall, the course was worth the money and I would come again next summer.
sent: I attended the summer course in July.
I was in the elementary group.
The speaking games helped me most.
I spoke more in two weeks than in a year.
Our teacher corrected mistakes at the end.
The grammar tests were too long.
We never had time to check the answers.
I suggest making the test shorter.
Overall, the course was worth the money.
I would come again next summer.
topics: The speaking games in the first hour did more for me than a year at school.
One part of the course clearly worked.
The Friday tests were long and we never checked the answers.
One part of the course clearly did not.
Make the test shorter and keep twenty minutes for the answers.
My suggestion is small and specific.
seeds.title: Feedback on a course
seeds.sub: What worked, what did not, what to change

seeds.goal: You can write from a city you are visiting: what you saw, what surprised you, what you ate and what you would do differently.
seeds.why: Travel writing at A2 is about impressions, not lists. One surprise is worth five monuments.
seeds.ex: Elmira's postcard from Istanbul was read out in class because of one sentence about the smell of the ferry.
seeds.read: Read the postcard and find one thing: what surprised Elmira most about the city?
seeds.task: Write a postcard from a city you are visiting (50–80 words): where you are, one thing you saw, one surprise, one thing you ate, and one plan for tomorrow.
model: We arrived in Istanbul on Tuesday and we are staying near the port.
Yesterday we walked around the old city for six hours and my legs still hurt.
What surprised me most is how many cats live in the streets — everybody feeds them.
We ate fish sandwiches by the water; they cost almost nothing and they were perfect.
Say what you will do next
Tomorrow we are taking the ferry to the Asian side.
I will bring you tea from the market. Love, Elmira.
sent: We arrived in Istanbul on Tuesday.
We are staying near the port.
Yesterday we walked around the old city.
My legs still hurt from the walking.
Many cats live in the streets here.
Everybody feeds them and nobody owns them.
We ate fish sandwiches by the water.
Tomorrow we are taking the ferry.
I have never seen a city like this.
I will bring you tea from the market.
topics: Six hours in the old city and my legs still hurt.
Yesterday was all walking.
Cats are everywhere and everybody feeds them.
One thing about this city I did not expect.
Fish sandwiches by the water, almost free and perfect.
The best meal was the cheapest.
ideas: The price of the plane ticket
A complaint about the hotel wifi
seeds.title: A postcard from a city
seeds.sub: A city in five impressions

seeds.goal: You can write a public notice: what the club or event is, who it is for, when and where it meets, what to bring and how to join.
seeds.why: A notice is read in four seconds. If the key facts are not visible at once, nobody comes.
seeds.ex: Nurbek's notice about a film club filled the room. The one before it, without a time, brought two people.
seeds.read: Read the notice and find one thing: what should a student bring to the first meeting?
seeds.task: Write a notice for the school noticeboard about a new club (50–80 words): what it is, who it is for, when and where, what happens there, what to bring, and how to join.
model: Give the notice a clear title
New: English Film Club, from 3 October.
Every Thursday we watch one film in English with subtitles and talk about it for half an hour.
The club is open to students of class 8 and above, at any level of English.
We meet in room 214 from four to six in the afternoon.
The rule is simple: during the discussion we speak only English, mistakes included.
Bring a notebook for new words, and tea if you want.
To join, write your name on the list on the door of room 214 before Wednesday.
phr: We meet in room … from … to …
Мы встречаемся в кабинете … с … до …
To join, write your name on …
sent: Every Thursday we watch a film in English.
The club is open to class 8 and above.
We meet in room 214 from four to six.
During the discussion we speak only English.
Bring a notebook for new words.
Write your name on the list before Wednesday.
The films which we choose have subtitles.
You do not need a high level of English.
Last year twenty students joined the club.
The first meeting will be on 3 October.
topics: A film in English with subtitles, then half an hour of discussion.
This is what happens at every meeting.
Room 214, Thursdays, four to six, from 3 October.
The practical details fit in one line.
Bring a notebook, write your name on the door list before Wednesday.
Joining takes ten seconds.
ideas: A list of my favourite films
My opinion about the school building
seeds.title: A notice for the noticeboard
seeds.sub: Get people to join in

connTable.hint: You add a second point of the same kind.
The second idea works against the first one.
You put the events of a story in order.

connItems.a: I wanted to come to your party.
connItems.b: , I had to work on Saturday.
connItems.why: However opens a sentence that works against the one before it.

connItems.a: We arrived at the hotel at six.
connItems.b: , we went straight to the beach.
connItems.why: After that puts the second event later in time.
Because gives the reason inside one sentence.

connItems.a: The café was small and noisy.
connItems.why: You admit a problem and then give the positive side.
But joins a good point and a bad point in one sentence.

connItems.a: First we visited the old town.
connItems.b: , we had lunch near the river.
connItems.why: A story needs time words to stay clear.

connItems.a: The film was three hours long
connItems.why: Although shows that the second fact is a surprise.
Also adds one more reason to like it.

connItems.b: I wrote my homework by hand.
connItems.why: So introduces the result of the first fact.

connItems.a: We booked the tickets in May
connItems.why: Because explains a decision you made.

connItems.b: , we waited forty minutes for our food.
connItems.why: However lets you be fair: one good point, one bad point.
And then joins two actions in the order they happened.
Although marks the contrast between problem and result.

tr.src: I was late. The bus did not come.
ans: I was late because the bus did not come.
tr.why: Because turns two short sentences into one clear idea.

tr.src: The hotel was cheap. It was clean.
ans: Although the hotel was cheap, it was clean.
tr.why: Although shows that the second fact is unexpected.

tr.src: We go to the museum and see the old maps.
ans: We went to the museum and saw the old maps.
tr.why: A story about yesterday keeps every verb in the past.
Experience up to now takes Present Perfect: I have never visited.

ans: Could you send me the photos, please?
tr.why: Could you…? turns an order into a request.

tr.src: I will visit my aunt next week. It is my plan.
ans: I am going to visit my aunt next week.
tr.why: Going to is for plans you have already made.

tr.cue: Add an adjective and a detail
ans: It was a small wooden house near the river.
tr.why: One adjective and one place detail change a bare sentence into a picture.

tr.src: The shop was open on Sunday.
ans: The shop was not open on Sunday.
The shop wasn't open on Sunday.
tr.why: Was not is the negative of was — no do is needed.

tr.src: The film was boring, because I left.
ans: The film was boring, so I left.
tr.why: Because gives the reason, so gives the result. They face opposite ways.

tr.src: In the room two beds and a table.
ans: There were two beds and a table in the room.
tr.why: Plural nouns take there were, not there was.

tr.src: This café is good. That café is not so good.
ans: This café is better than that one.
tr.why: A comparison needs the comparative form plus than.

ans: I will come at half past seven.
tr.why: Later means nothing to the reader; a time does.

reg.inf: I do not really agree with this.
reg.why: A blog comment is everyday English, not a legal document.

reg.ctx: A note of apology to a neighbour
reg.fm: I am sorry about the noise last night.
reg.why: An apology loses its value in chat abbreviations.

reg.fm: The service was slow but polite.
reg.why: A review is read by strangers, so it keeps a calm voice.

reg.fm: I would like to inform you of my arrival.
reg.inf: I arrive on Friday at six.
reg.why: With a friend, facts beat formulas.

reg.fm: Could I hand in my essay on Monday?
reg.inf: can i give the essay monday
reg.why: A request to a teacher keeps capital letters and a question mark.

reg.ctx: A story for the school magazine
reg.fm: It was the best day of the summer.
reg.why: Slang ages fast and closes the text to many readers.

reg.fm: I regret that I am unable to join you.
reg.why: Between friends short is warm; long is cold.

reg.ctx: A description for a school website
reg.fm: Our school has a new library.
reg.inf: our school got a cool new library
reg.why: A public page needs neutral words: has, not got.

reg.ctx: A note to your host family
reg.fm: Thank you for the wonderful dinner.
reg.why: A thank-you note is short but complete.

reg.fm: I would like to state that this is beautiful.
reg.why: A comment is spoken English written down.

reg.fm: I would like to book a double room.
reg.inf: I need a room, two people, ok?
reg.why: A booking is business: it needs the standard formula.

reg.ctx: A message in a group chat
reg.fm: Please be advised that the meeting starts at five.
reg.inf: We start at five, see you!
reg.why: Office language in a friends' chat sounds like a joke.

opts: Two facts the reader can use.
imp.why: Nice is the word people use when they remember nothing.

imp.sent: The food in the café was bad.
imp.why: In a review, details are what make the reader trust you.

imp.sent: We had a very good time.
opts: Busy is not the same as enjoyable.
imp.why: Very + adjective is the weakest form of praise.

opts: Two weak words instead of one strong one.
imp.why: Strong adjectives do not need very in front of them.

imp.sent: He is a very good teacher.
opts: Says what he actually does well.
imp.why: Name the quality, do not rate it.

imp.sent: I was very angry about the delay.
opts: Strong but controlled — right for writing.
Spoken and a little rude in writing.
imp.why: In writing, a controlled word is stronger than a loud one.

opts: The exact word for very small.
imp.why: English has a single word for most very + adjective pairs.

imp.sent: We walked a lot in the old town.
opts: A number the reader can imagine.
Much is not used like this in a positive sentence.
imp.why: Time and numbers make a story concrete.

opts: One word: you could not stop reading.
A negative instead of a description.
imp.why: Interesting is the most-used and least-informative adjective in reviews.

imp.sent: The staff were bad to us.
imp.why: Behaviour words are precise: rude, slow, unhelpful.

imp.sent: I think this place is good for families.
opts: ideal for families with small children
imp.ans: ideal for families with small children
imp.why: A recommendation needs an exact audience.

imp.sent: The weather was very bad all week.
imp.why: Describe the weather, do not rate it.

tl.long: I am writing this email to you in order to tell you about my holiday in Turkey.
tl.model: I want to tell you about my holiday.
tl.why: 'I am writing this email in order to' is four words of nothing.

tl.long: The café that we visited was a place that was very close to our hotel.
tl.model: The café was very close to our hotel.
tl.why: 'A place that was' can always be deleted.

tl.long: There were a lot of people there and because of that the queue was very long.
tl.model: The queue was long because of the crowd.
tl.why: Two clauses become one when you use because of + noun.

tl.long: In my opinion I think that this restaurant is good for a family dinner.
tl.model: This restaurant is good for a family dinner.
tl.why: 'In my opinion I think' says the same thing twice.

tl.long: The reason why I did not come to your party is that I was ill on that day.
tl.model: I did not come because I was ill.
tl.why: 'The reason why … is that' is a long way to say because.

tl.long: We stayed in a hotel which was situated in the centre of the old city.
tl.model: We stayed in a hotel in the old city centre.
tl.why: 'Which was situated in' becomes a simple preposition.

tl.long: It is very important to say that the staff were polite to all the guests.
tl.model: The staff were polite to every guest.
tl.why: If it is important, just say it — do not announce it.

tl.long: I would like to recommend this place to people who like quiet places.
tl.model: I recommend this place to people who like quiet.
tl.why: 'I would like to recommend' is one verb too many.

tl.long: After we had finished our dinner we decided that we would go for a walk.
tl.model: After dinner we went for a walk.
tl.why: 'Decided that we would' hides the action itself.

tl.long: The thing which I did not like about the hotel was the noise at night.
tl.model: I did not like the noise at night.
tl.why: 'The thing which I did not like was' is a slow start.

distract: My cousin is studying medicine in Poland.
The paragraph is about your topic, not about a relative's studies.
I have been learning English for three years.
Information about you as a learner does not belong in the text.
The train to Almaty leaves at midnight.
A timetable detail with no link to this paragraph.
My father bought a new car in April.
A family purchase changes the subject.
I usually go to bed before eleven.
A daily habit that does not develop the topic.
The film we watched had a strange ending.
A different text, a different subject.
My laptop is quite old but it still works.
Your equipment is not part of this story.
We have two cats and a parrot at home.
Pets belong to another paragraph.
I paid for the tickets with my mother's card.
A payment detail nobody asked about.
My best friend moved to Astana last year.
A friend's move is another story.
The bakery near my house opens at seven.
Opening hours are off topic here.
I am going to buy a bike next month.
A future plan inside a paragraph about something else.

topics.body: The rooms were clean and the beds were comfortable. The breakfast started at seven every morning.
topics.right: The hotel itself was a pleasant surprise.

topics.body: We waited twenty minutes for a table and another half an hour for the food.
topics.right: The service was the weakest part of the evening.

topics.body: He always listens first and only then gives advice. He never laughs at my mistakes.
topics.right: This is why I trust my older brother.

topics.body: It rained on four days out of seven and the wind was cold in the evenings.
topics.right: The weather was the only real problem of the trip.

topics.body: First you fry the onion for two minutes. Then you add rice, water and salt.
topics.right: Making plov at home is easier than it sounds.

topics.body: There is a park, two cafés and a small cinema in the same street.
topics.right: My district has everything you need for a weekend.

topics.body: She spent the whole evening helping me and did not take any money for it.
topics.right: My neighbour did something I did not expect.

topics.body: The seats were narrow and there was no space for our bags.
topics.right: The bus journey itself was uncomfortable.

tsWrong: The city has a long history.
I do not usually write reviews.
My English teacher is from Canada.
I would like to go there again next year.
The photos on the website are beautiful.
offIdeas: The price of my bus ticket
A detail that changes nothing for the reader of this text.
What my brother thinks about the topic
Another person's opinion weakens your own text.
A long description of the weather
Weather is background, not content, unless the task asks for it.
My marks at school last term
School results have no place in this genre.
The name of the hotel receptionist
A private detail that helps nobody.
How long the journey took by car
Travel time is off the point here.
What I watched on the plane
An entertaining detail that takes the reader away.

outlineRules.msg: The opening line names the subject: a reader who does not know the topic stops after one sentence.
The closing part sums up or asks — it never introduces a new fact.

rubric.task: Did you cover every point of the task and keep to the genre?
rubric.organisation: One paragraph, one idea, and linking words between the sentences.
rubric.vocabulary: Topic words and precise adjectives instead of good, bad and nice.
rubric.grammar: Past forms, articles, prepositions and subject-verb agreement.
